| **插件市场**（dsh-market） | 一个**第三方社区插件**，它有自己的插件目录与详情页 | ⏳ 需先被该目录收录（见下文） |

两者的关系是：插件市场本身也是装在「插件」页里的一个插件。它展示什么，取决于它自己的目录文件，与内置的「添加插件」无关。

**所以：现在就能装，用第一种方式。** 想让它出现在插件市场里被搜到，需要走第三种方式（提交收录）。

---

## 安装

### 第 1 步：在「插件」页添加（现在就能用）

1. 打开 Harness → **设置**
2. 进入 **插件**（内置的那一页，不是插件市场）
3. 点 **「添加插件」**
4. 在弹出的输入框里填下面任意一种：

   ```
   https://github.com/YSDLNGF/dsh-acrylic
   ```

   也接受这几种等价写法：

   ```
   https://github.com/YSDLNGF/dsh-acrylic.git
   github:YSDLNGF/dsh-acrylic
   ```

   > 输入框提示是「输入插件的包名、GitHub 仓库地址或本地目录路径」。
   > 本插件尚未发布到 npm，所以请用 **GitHub 地址**，不要填包名。

5. 点「安装」，确认来源，Harness 会自己 clone 到
   `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-acrylic`、登记 `bundles`，然后提示重启

重启后进入 **设置 → 通用 → 透明亚克力**，看到滑块就说明页面那半边成功了。

> **安装格式依据**：`@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-manager` 的 `parseInstallSpec()`
> 接受 npm 包名、`file:`/绝对路径、`*.tgz`、以及 git 地址
> （`github:owner/repo`、`git+https://…`、或宿主仓库 URL）。
> 本仓库根 `package.json` 已声明 `dsh.bundle`，满足「可安装」的判定条件。

### 第 2 步：让窗口透出壁纸（这一步需要命令行）

第 1 步只让页面半透明，但窗口本身还是不透明的 —— 壁纸透不出来。
窗口材质是 Electron `BrowserWindow` 的**构造参数**，只存在于主进程，
插件（运行在渲染进程侧）碰不到窗口对象，所以必须改 `app.asar`。

这与现有同类插件（如 [dsh-desktop-glass](https://github.com/JianHeShui/dsh-desktop-glass)）
的处境相同，**没有纯插件方案**。

```powershell
cd dsh-acrylic
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\apply-when-closed.ps1
```

这个脚本会：

1. 等你从托盘退出 Harness（它监测 `app.asar` 锁释放）
2. 自动给 `app.asar` 打**等字节补丁**（主窗口加 `backgroundMaterial: acrylic`）
3. 自动重启 Harness

**你只需要退出一次，剩下它自己完成。**

做完这步，窗口才能真正透出壁纸。

### 第 3 步：让它出现在插件市场（可选）

插件市场（dsh-market）的插件列表来自一份目录文件，托管在社区仓库
[awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin)。
**要被市场搜到，必须向那个仓库提交一个条目文件。** 这不是自动的。

收录要求与当前状态：

| 要求 | 状态 |
| --- | --- |
| 根 `package.json` 声明 `dsh.bundle` | ✅ `./plugin/cordis.patch.yml` |
| 仓库有真实可用代码 | ✅ |
| `screenshots.json` + 截图 | ✅ `assets/screenshot-1.jpg` |
| 仓库 topic `dsh-plugin` | ✅ 已添加 |
| 仓库创建满 1 天 | 由对方 CI 检查 |
| 条目文件 | ⏳ 待提交 PR |

需要提交的文件（单个 YAML，放在对方仓库 `data/plugins/` 下）：

**`data/plugins/YSDLNGF__dsh-acrylic.yml`**

```yaml
url: https://github.com/YSDLNGF/dsh-acrylic
name: YSDLNGF/dsh-acrylic
category: theme
description:
  en: Windows Acrylic window material plus layered frosted panels for the DeepSeek Harness desktop app.
  zh: DeepSeek Harness 桌面版的 Windows 亚克力窗口材质与分层雾面效果。
```

分类选 `theme` 的话，合并后会进入插件市场的**「主题」Tab**，
支持一键安装、切换、卸载。

合并后官网自动重建，市场里就能搜到了。

---

## 卸载

**只卸载插件（保留窗口补丁）**：设置 → **插件**（内置那页），
找到 `dsh-acrylic`，点「卸载」。

**连同窗口材质一起还原**：

```powershell
node uninstall.mjs
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\restore-asar.ps1
```

两者都做完再重启，恢复原生外观。

---

## 调参

两种方式，均**实时生效，无需重启**：

**控制台**（F12 → Console）：

```js
glass()                      // 看当前参数
glass({ alpha: 92 })         // 浮层/输入栏厚度，越大越实
glass({ noise: 4 })          // 亚克力颗粒感
glass({ enabled: false })    // 一键关闭
glass.reset()                // 回默认
```

**设置页**：`设置 → 通用 → 透明亚克力`，带滑块。

| 参数 | 默认 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alpha` | 92 | 浮层与输入栏的雾面厚度。92 是实测最平衡的一档 |
| `noise` | 3.2 | 亚克力细微噪点，纯色平板没有"薄"感 |

改色值请直接编辑 `plugin/client.js` 顶部的 `GLASS_STYLE`，每个值旁都注明了由来。

---

## 已知限制

- **窗口材质补丁在 Harness 更新后失效**。更新会覆盖 `app.asar`，
  重跑一次 `apply-when-closed.ps1` 即可。
- **插件市场至今搜不到**：本插件尚未被
  [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin)
  目录收录，因此第三方市场「插件市场」（dsh-market）里搜不到。
  收录需要向该仓库提交 PR（见「第 3 步」）。
  **这不影响安装** —— 用内置「插件」页的「添加插件」粘 GitHub 地址即可。
- **改的是宿主程序**。请自行评估风险；本仓库提供备份与还原路径，
  且补丁脚本在锚点不匹配时会直接退出、不动已安装文件。
- **Acrylic 失焦会变实**。Windows 降级材质行为，无法绕过。
  介意可改用 `-Material mica`。

---

## 需要自己编译安装吗

不需要。本仓库是**即插即用**的 DSH 插件，不是需要 build 的前端项目：

| 文件 | 作用 | 需要编译吗 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `package.json` | 根 manifest（声明 `dsh.bundle`，供市场/命令行安装） | ❌ |
| `plugin/` | 插件本体（页面半边） | ❌ 直接复制 |
| `patch-asar.mjs` | 改 `app.asar` 的工具 | ❌ Node 直接跑 |
| `apply-when-closed.ps1` | 自动化：等退出→打补丁→重启 | ❌ |
| `install.mjs` / `uninstall.mjs` | 命令行方式装卸 | ❌ |

用 Node 18+ 和 PowerShell 即可，**没有构建步骤**。

---

## 关于本项目

**本项目的代码与文档全部由 AI 编写。**

从用户一句"我想让 harness 有透明轻薄亚克力效果"开始，
确认需求、逆向 `main.js` 里的窗口参数、发现 `backgroundColor` 与
`backgroundMaterial` 互斥、逐层定位"发灰"来源、把侧栏收起按钮位移的
bug 定位到 `backdrop-filter` 创建包含块、到最终的分层雾面方案 ——
包括 `plugin/client.js` 里的每一条规则、每一个数值、这几百行中文注释，
以及这份 README，都出自 AI Agent 之手（与用户多轮协作完成）。

**也走了不少弯路。** 曾经连续多轮在错误假设上打转，以为调
`backdrop-filter` 的 blur 值就能糊掉背后的文字，直到做像素测量才发现
它从未生效；也曾把"插件市场"和内置的"添加插件"混为一谈，
写出了错误的安装说明。这些失败结论都被写进了代码注释和「已知限制」，
因为**知道什么行不通，和知道什么行得通同样有用**。

如果你也在做类似的事，希望这个仓库能替你省掉那些来回试错的夜晚。

欢迎提交 Issue 或 PR。

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE)

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: semantic recall of what you already said in earlier sessions of the same workspace, appended to the conversation and available as an on-demand tool.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-lembrar

Semantic recall of what you already said, inside
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).

An agent starts every session knowing nothing that happened in the previous
ones. `dsh-lembrar` indexes your own messages (`user/message` events) from earlier
sessions of the same workspace and puts the matching ones back in front of the
agent: once automatically before each turn, and on demand through a tool. Matching
is by meaning, not by exact words.

It is recall, not a diary or a summary: the indexed text is your raw message, and
what comes back is the excerpt plus the session id and event sequence number, so
the agent can open the original event with the harness session tools.

## Install

```sh
# 1. pnpm — the harness manages profile plugins with it
npm install -g pnpm

# 2. add the plugin to your `web` profile
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-lembrar

# 3. restart the harness: the bundle layer is read at boot
#    stop `dsh web` (Ctrl+C) and start it again
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

If `dsh` is already installed globally, step 2 is
`dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-lembrar`.

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` appends the plugin
row to the profile bundle list. That row is the only activation, and it is
applied at every boot.

Check the loaded line:

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A10 lembrar
```

Expected shape:

```yaml
- id: lembrar
  name: dsh-lembrar
  config:
    colecao: sessoes-bgem3-v1
    injetar: true
    ...
```

### Update and uninstall

```sh
# update: re-run the add command, then restart the harness
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-lembrar

# uninstall
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-lembrar
# then restart the harness
```

## Requirements

- **Node.js** `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the same range DeepSeek Harness supports).
- **pnpm** on `PATH` — the harness uses it to manage profile plugins.
- **DeepSeek Harness** with session history indexed. The `web` profile mounts
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query-sqlite`, which maintains
  `~/.dsh/storages/session-search.db`; `dsh-lembrar` reads that database for the
  session list. Without it there is no past to search, and the plugin stays
  silent.
- **memsearch** with local ONNX embeddings for the vector index:
  `uv tool install "memsearch[onnx]"` (or `pipx install "memsearch[onnx]"`).
  Point the plugin at the binary when it is not named `memsearch` on `PATH`
  (`LEMBRAR_MEMSEARCH` or the `memsearch` config key).
- **sqlite3** CLI on `PATH` (the plugin reads the session list with it).
- **Python 3** to export the corpus (standard library only; `exportar.py`).
- Optional: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-session-query` for the `session_event_read`
  tool the skill mentions when an excerpt is not enough.

The plugin itself is plain ESM using only Node built-ins: no build step and no
native dependency.

## Build the index

`dsh-lembrar` reads an existing memsearch collection; it does not embed anything
itself. The package ships the two commands that turn the harness session database
into that collection:

```sh
# where the installed package lives (adjust if your profile has another name)
PKG="$HOME/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/dsh-lembrar"
STATE="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/dsh-lembrar"

# 1. one markdown file per user message, from session-search.db
python3 "$PKG/scripts/exportar.py" --destino "$STATE/corpus"

# 2. embed them (only new or changed text is embedded; `--force` redoes all)
memsearch index "$STATE/corpus" -c sessoes-bgem3-v1

# 3. write the marker the plugin checks before it searches
"$PKG/scripts/marcar-indice.sh"
```

The three lines are idempotent. After the first full run, a refresh takes
seconds when little has changed, so it is reasonable to run them from cron or a
systemd timer (for example, once a day):

```sh
0 3 * * * PKG="$HOME/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/dsh-lembrar" STATE="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/dsh-lembrar"; python3 "$PKG/scripts/exportar.py" --destino "$STATE/corpus" && memsearch index "$STATE/corpus" -c sessoes-bgem3-v1 && "$PKG/scripts/marcar-indice.sh"
```

The marker is a small JSON file in `<estadoDir>/<colecao>.json`. It exists so the
hook never pays a failed search for an index that was never built: run the
indexer without step 3 and the plugin keeps quiet.

The collection name is the contract between the index and the plugin: it
defaults to `sessoes-bgem3-v1` on both sides and is configurable.

## Configuration

Every path is configurable and the defaults derive from your home directory, so
nothing is tied to a specific machine. Override by environment variable, or by
the config of the `lembrar` line in your profile patch. A patch replaces the
whole config of the line, so restate every key you want to keep.

| Config key | Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `colecao` | — | `sessoes-bgem3-v1` | memsearch collection |
| `injetar` | — | `true` | append memories to each turn via `agent/pre-step` |
| `maxTokens` | — | `800` | token cap for the appended block (~4 characters per token) |
| `k` | — | `8` | events returned by one search, before the token cut |
| `scoreMinimo` | — | `0.55` | similarity floor; below it the hook stays silent |
| `buscarHabilitado` | — | `true` | register the on-demand `lembrar` tool |
| `buscarTimeoutMs` | — | `30000` | engine timeout per search |
| `exigirMesmoCwd` | — | `true` | only sessions with the caller's exact `cwd` are authorized |
| `estadoDir` | `LEMBRAR_ESTADO_DIR` | `$XDG_STATE_HOME/dsh-lembrar/.estado`, or `<package>/.lembrar/.estado` for a local `link:` install | where the index marker lives |
| `banco` | `LEMBRAR_BANCO` | `~/.dsh/storages/session-search.db` | session database |
| `memsearch` | `LEMBRAR_MEMSEARCH` | `memsearch` on `PATH` | search engine binary |

Profile patch example (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: lembrar
  config:
    colecao: sessoes-bgem3-v1
    estadoDir: '/home/you/.local/state/dsh-lembrar/.estado'
```

## Usage

You do not call anything. On the first step of each turn the hook searches your
current message against the index, keeps the hits above the floor, and appends a
short block at the **end** of the message list. Appending (never rewriting an
earlier message) is what preserves the prompt prefix cache: only the new suffix
is paid for. When nothing matches, the decision comes back untouched and the turn
costs zero extra tokens.

The agent can also search on demand with the `lembrar` tool:

```text
lembrar { "consulta": "what did we decide about the backup schedule" }
```

Each hit returns `session_id`, `seq` and the excerpt. The `lembrar-recall` skill
describes the follow-up: open the original event with `session_event_read` when
the excerpt is not enough.

## Privacy and authorization

- **Same workspace only.** A session only sees sessions whose `cwd` matches its
  own exactly, read from `persisted_sessions`. If that list cannot be read, no
  hit is authorized: the failure is closed, not open.
- **No `cwd`, no memory.** Headless, CLI and subagent sessions without a `cwd`
  receive nothing; with `exigirMesmoCwd: false` you can disable the gate
  explicitly.
- **Secret directories stay out.** A session whose `cwd` is inside a `segredos/`
  or `vault/` directory is excluded from the corpus and cannot be a caller.
- **Your words only.** The corpus is limited to `user/message` events from the
  `current` surface. Assistant messages and tool payloads are never indexed, and
  messages injected by plugins or by the host are filtered out.
- **Local by default.** The index is a local Milvus Lite database
  (`~/.memsearch/milvus.db`); the embeddings run locally.

## Verification

From a clone of the repository (tests are not part of the installed tarball):

```sh
node --test tests/*.test.js
```

The suite covers authorization by `cwd`, secret-path exclusion, appending without
rewriting, silence when there is no signal, the token budget, one excerpt per
session, engine failure handling and the tool/

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: one on-demand tool that finds tools and skills outside the agent schema by meaning and registers the found tool in the requesting scope.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-alfandega

On-demand tool catalog for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).

A profile with many plugins and MCP servers sends hundreds of tool definitions on
every request. Every definition costs schema tokens for every turn, and a tool
list that large is well past the point where model accuracy starts to drop.
`dsh-alfandega` adds **one** tool, `achar_ferramenta` ("find tool" in
Portuguese), that finds the tool or skill missing from the agent schema by
meaning and registers the found tool in the requesting agent's scope. The agent
discovers the capability as content, when it needs it, instead of carrying every
schema all the time.

| Who | Surface | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| the agent | `achar_ferramenta` tool | the full schema of the matching tool, plus registration in its scope |
| you, in the chat | `/alfandega <what you want to do>` | the same search, as text |

## Install

```sh
# 1. pnpm (needed by `dsh plugin`)
npm install -g pnpm

# 2. add the plugin to your `web` profile
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-alfandega
```

If `dsh` is already installed globally, step 2 is:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-alfandega
```

Restart the harness after installing: the bundle layer is read at boot.

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

Check that the line was loaded:

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A4 alfandega
```

Expected shape:

```yaml
- id: alfandega
  name: dsh-alfandega
  config:
    colecao: ferramentas-bgem3-v1
    topK: 5
    buscaTimeoutMs: 20000
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` appends
`dsh-alfandega` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile manifest. That line is
the only activation.

### Update and uninstall

```sh
# update: re-run the add command, then restart the harness
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-alfandega

# uninstall, then restart
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-alfandega
```

## What the plugin does

```
the model needs a capability that is not in its schema
        │
        ▼
achar_ferramenta(consulta)                ← one tool, always in the schema
        │
        ├─ 1. optional vector search in a memsearch collection, by MEANING
        ├─ 2. completed by local lexical ranking (name > description > keyword)
        │
        ▼
returns the FULL schema as CONTENT (the prompt prefix is not rewritten)
and registers the tool in the scope of the agent that asked
        │
        ▼
the tool is callable from the NEXT request on — one cache re-warm, not one
per request
```

- **One tool.** `achar_ferramenta({ consulta, quantas? })`.
- **One command.** `/alfandega <what you want to do>`; `/alfandega` alone
  reports the catalog size and path.
- **One hook.** `tools/change` clears the in-memory catalog cache.
- **No UI, no client bundle, no network service.** `client.js` does not exist
  on purpose.

Registration is agent-scoped (`exec.agent.ctx.tools.register`), never global:
the tool array of the prompt prefix is extended once, when the model asks, so
the prompt cache survives.

## Requirements

- **Node.js** `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the range DeepSeek Harness supports).
- **pnpm** on `PATH`; the harness manages profile plugins with it.
- **DeepSeek Harness** itself, e.g. `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`.
- **memsearch** is optional. With it, the first ranking stage is vector search
  over a collection whose item ids follow `ferramenta-<name>` /
  `skill-<name>`. Without it (or with the index busy/unavailable), the plugin
  falls back to local lexical ranking and says so in the result. Nothing breaks.

## The catalog is generated on your machine

The package deliberately ships **no catalog**. A catalog is a dump of the tool
and skill registry of one machine; shipping it would leak that machine's paths
and internal descriptions, and it would be stale for everyone else.

On the first call (`achar_ferramenta` or `/alfandega`), if there is no catalog
at the configured path, the plugin:

1. reads the live tool registry (`tools.schemas()`),
2. lists the skills visible to the calling agent,
3. writes the catalog to the configured path and answers from it.

Default path: `~/.dsh/alfandega/catalogo.json`. If the directory is not
writable, the plugin keeps the catalog in memory for the session and logs a
warning instead of failing.

To refresh the catalog (for example after installing a new plugin), delete the
file and call the tool again:

```sh
rm ~/.dsh/alfandega/catalogo.json
```

The search also merges what the calling agent already sees, so a tool that is in
the schema never appears twice or gets registered again. The hook
`tools/change` clears the in-memory cache, so a regenerated file is picked up
without a restart.

## Configuration

All keys live on the `alfandega` line of the profile patch. A patch replaces the
whole config of the line, so restate every key you want to keep.

| Key | Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `catalogo` | `DSH_ALFANDEGA_CATALOGO` | `~/.dsh/alfandega/catalogo.json` | catalog path; `~/` is expanded |
| `colecao` | — | `ferramentas-bgem3-v1` | memsearch collection queried for vector search |
| `topK` | — | `5` | how many items a call returns (capped at 20) |
| `buscaTimeoutMs` | — | `20000` | vector search ceiling; on timeout the lexical ranking answers |

Profile patch example (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: alfandega
  config:
    colecao: 'ferramentas-bgem3-v1'
    catalogo: '/home/you/.dsh/alfandega/catalogo.json'
    topK: 5
    buscaTimeoutMs: 20000
```

When developing the plugin from a directory, a `catalogo.json` next to
`index.js` takes precedence over the home default; that is how a checkout can
keep a pre-generated catalog while a package install generates its own.

## Usage

Ask the agent for a capability it does not seem to have ("run a long command in
the background", "search the web", "start a workflow"). It calls
`achar_ferramenta` and receives the full schema of the match.

In the chat:

```sh
/alfandega list background jobs      # find and show the matching tool
/alfandega                           # catalog size, path and state
```

What a result looks like:

```
[alfandega] 1 de 42 itens para "list background jobs" (lexical + registro sob demanda).

FERRAMENTA job_list
  List background jobs started by this session
  parâmetros:
    { ... }

registradas agora no seu escopo: job_list. Elas ficam disponíveis a partir da
PRÓXIMA requisição.
```

## Verification

From a clone of the repository:

```sh
node --test tests/
```

The suite covers the lexical ranking, vector-first ordering, scoped
registration (never twice, never global), the frame-format JSON Schema,
catalog read errors, catalog generation at the destination, and the package
contract. It needs no harness install and no index; when
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` is resolvable (or `DSH_TOOLS_ENTRY` points at its
entrypoint), it also validates the registered schema with the harness compiler.

To verify the install: check the `dump-config` line above, restart the harness,
then run `/alfandega web search`. The first call reports
`catálogo gerado agora a partir do host`.

## Limits, stated

- **The catalog is a snapshot.** It is written on first use and does not update
  itself when a new tool appears. Delete the file to regenerate it. The
  `tools/change` hook only invalidates the in-memory cache.
- **Registration is not instantaneous for the model.** The tool becomes callable
  from the next request; in the current step the model already has the full
  schema as text, which is enough to decide.
- **Vector search is an accelerator, not a requirement.** Missing memsearch,
  missing collection, or a busy database means lexical ranking, which can order
  results worse but still returns them.
- **Skills do not become tools.** A found skill is returned with a pointer and is
  loaded through the harness `skill` tool, which owns the skill catalog.
- **One tool, on purpose.** The plugin does not add a second model-facing tool;
  the whole point is

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: semantic search over the AGENTS.md and README.md rules of your workspace tree, with a tool for the agent and a command for you.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-regras

Semantic search over the Markdown rules of a directory tree, inside
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).

`AGENTS.md` and `README.md` are where an agent learns how a repository works.
`dsh-regras` indexes those files with [memsearch](https://github.com/zilliztech/memsearch)
and gives the agent a tool to find the rule that applies to the task in front of
it, with the real file path and line range so it can open the source. A command
adds a hygiene report: duplicate candidates, path references that no longer
exist, and docs that stopped while the code moved.

One plugin line, two surfaces:

| Who | How | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| the agent | `qual_regra` tool | the rule segments for the task, with the **real path** and line range |
| you, in the chat | `/regras [higiene \| pares \| buscar <termo>]` | the hygiene report or a rule search |

## Requirements

- **Node.js** `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the same range DeepSeek Harness supports).
- **pnpm** on `PATH`; the harness manages profile plugins with it.
- **DeepSeek Harness** itself, e.g. `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`.
- **memsearch** for the index, with the local ONNX embeddings extra:
  `uv tool install "memsearch[onnx]"` (or `pipx install "memsearch[onnx]"`).

The `qual_regra` tool is plain Node.js. The `/regras` hygiene report is a bash
plus Python script (`relatorio.sh` calls `relatorio.py`), so it runs on Linux and
macOS; on Windows, run it from WSL or Git Bash with Python available.

## Install

```sh
# 1. pnpm (needed by `dsh plugin`)
npm install -g pnpm

# 2. add the plugin to your `web` profile
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-regras

# 3. restart the harness: the bundle layer is read at boot
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

If `dsh` is already installed globally, step 2 is
`dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-regras`.

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` appends
`dsh-regras` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile manifest. That line is the
only activation, and it is applied at every boot.

Check the loaded line:

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A3 regras
```

Expected shape:

```yaml
- id: regras
  name: dsh-regras
  config: {}
```

### Update and uninstall

```sh
# update: re-run the add command, then restart the harness
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-regras   # uninstall, then restart
```

## Build the index

`dsh-regras` reads an existing memsearch collection; it does not embed anything
itself. Index the tree that holds your rules once:

```sh
memsearch index ~/workspaces -c regras-bgem3-v1
memsearch stats -c regras-bgem3-v1
```

The command indexes every Markdown file below the tree. If you want only
`AGENTS.md` and `README.md`, give `memsearch index` a directory that contains
just those files (a symlink mirror works). The plugin resolves each hit through
`realpath`, so the answer always cites the real file, not the mirror.

The collection name is the contract between the index and the plugin: it defaults
to `regras-bgem3-v1` and is configurable on both sides.

## Configuration

Every path is configurable and the defaults derive from your home directory, so
nothing is tied to a specific machine. Override by environment variable, or by
the config of the `regras` line in your profile patch. A patch replaces the
whole config of the line, so restate every key you want to keep.

| Config key | Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `raiz` | `DSH_REGRAS_RAIZ` | `~/workspaces` | root of the rules tree |
| `colecao` | `DSH_REGRAS_COLECAO` | `regras-bgem3-v1` | memsearch collection |
| `memsearch` | `DSH_REGRAS_MEMSEARCH` | `~/.local/bin/memsearch` | memsearch binary |
| `espelho` | `DSH_REGRAS_ESPELHO` | `<package>/.espelho`, else `raiz` | corpus scanned by the hygiene report |

The report also uses `DSH_REGRAS_PY` (a Python interpreter with `pymilvus` and
`numpy`); by default it uses the memsearch tool environment, then `python3`.

Profile patch example (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: regras
  config:
    raiz: '/home/you/rules'
    colecao: 'regras-bgem3-v1'
    memsearch: '/home/you/.local/bin/memsearch'
    espelho: '/home/you/rules'
```

## Usage

Ask the agent a question about where something belongs, how to name it, what is
forbidden, or who owns it. It calls `qual_regra` and gets the matching segments
with their source paths.

In the chat:

```sh
/regras buscar naming          # five best rule segments
/regras higiene                # duplicate candidates, orphan paths, doc/code drift
/regras pares                  # the candidate pairs, with both texts, for review
```

`higiene` writes `relatorios/<date>-higiene/` next to the package, with
`relatorio.md` and `pares-candidatos.jsonl`. The duplicate line is **candidates
only**: embeddings measure topical proximity, not contradiction, and two
opposite rules look alike in the vector space. The reader decides with both
texts in hand. Nothing is rewritten: the report only reads files.

## Verification

From a clone of the repository:

```sh
node --test tests/
python3 scripts/relatorio.py --selftest
```

The test suite covers the tool and command registration, real-path resolution,
secret-path rejection and the package contract. The report selftest covers path
citation, orphan detection, git drift and kNN. Neither needs the index.

To verify the install, check the `dump-config` output above and ask the agent
for a rule.

## Troubleshooting

- **`binário não encontrado: memsearch`** — install memsearch or point
  `DSH_REGRAS_MEMSEARCH` at the binary.
- **No results** — the collection is empty or has another name. Run
  `memsearch index <tree> -c <name>` and make the names match.
- **Report says `pymilvus indisponível`** — the interpreter running the report
  has no `pymilvus`. Set `DSH_REGRAS_PY` to the memsearch environment Python
  (`~/.local/share/uv/tools/memsearch/bin/python`) and restart the harness, or
  run `DSH_REGRAS_PY=<that-python> bash scripts/relatorio.sh` directly.
- **`pnpm not found on PATH`** — `npm install -g pnpm`, then re-run.
- **Plugin installed but nothing appears** — restart the harness; the bundle
  layer is read at boot, not at install time.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin that gives the agent eyes: capture a screen, measure drift, and check written expectations against the image with an embedding score.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-olhos

Eyes for an agent inside [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness):
capture a URL or a local HTML file, measure how much the screen drifted, and test
written expectations against the image in the same 768-dimensional embedding space.

Every verdict comes with its score. "The screen is fine" without a number is the
sentence this plugin exists to prevent.

One plugin line, two surfaces:

| Who | How | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| the agent | `olhos_verificar` tool | for each expectation: cosine score, confirmed or not, the capture path, and (opt-in) drift against the last reference |
| you, in the chat | `/olhos ...` | capture and compare, keep a good reference, or find an old capture by meaning |

## Install

```sh
npm install -g pnpm
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-olhos
```

Restart the harness: the bundle layer is read at boot. Then check the loaded line:

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A6 olhos
```

Expected shape:

```yaml
- id: olhos
  name: dsh-olhos
  config:
    capturas: temporarios/olhos
    limiar: 0.7344
    navegador: casa
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` appends `dsh-olhos`
to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile manifest. That line is the only
activation.

Update: re-run the add command and restart. Uninstall:
`npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-olhos`, then restart.

## Requirements

- **Node.js** `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the range DeepSeek Harness supports).
- **pnpm** on `PATH`; the harness uses it to manage profile plugins.
- **DeepSeek Harness** itself, for example `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`.
- **Python 3** on `PATH`, with **`websocket-client`** for the capture script:
  `python3 -m pip install websocket-client`.
- **Chrome or Chromium** listening on CDP. The default (`navegador: casa`)
  attaches to `http://127.0.0.1:9222`, so start the browser with
  `--remote-debugging-port=9222`. With `navegador: proprio` the plugin launches
  its own disposable headless browser (`OLHOS_CHROME`, default `google-chrome`)
  instead.
- **An EmbeddingGemma engine checkout**, which produces the scores. Point
  `OLHOS_GEMMA_RAIZ` at it (default `~/workspaces/tools/embeddinggemma`). The
  directory must contain `venv/bin/python`, `src/embeddinggemma.py`,
  `src/vetores.py`, and the model cache under `modelos/`. Its own install script
  builds the CPU environment (torch, sentence-transformers) and downloads the
  1.5 GB model.

The plugin does **not** bundle the embedding engine. Without that checkout a
capture still works, but no score can be produced, and `olhos_verificar` fails
with a message naming `OLHOS_GEMMA_RAIZ`.

The shell scripts (`.sh`) and Python companions run on Linux and macOS. On
Windows, use WSL or Git Bash with Python 3 available.

## Usage

Ask the agent to check something visible. It calls the tool with a target and one
expectation per line:

```text
Use olhos_verificar on http://127.0.0.1:3080/ with the expectations
"the panel shows three session cards" and "the error message is visible".
```

The tool answers with a score per expectation and a verdict:

```text
limiar 0.7344
| expectation                         | score  | verdict   |
| the panel shows three session cards | 0.7225 | not found |
| the error message is visible        | 0.6254 | not found |
0/2 confirmed. Lowest score 0.6254. Capture: temporarios/olhos/.../20261013-163453.png
```

The threshold is strict: a score must be **greater than** the threshold to
confirm. Scores below it are reported as not found, which is the deliberate
precision-over-recall bias described under [Limits](#limits).

In the chat:

```sh
/olhos http://127.0.0.1:3080/                       # capture and drift against the last reference
/olhos http://127.0.0.1:3080/ "three cards" "error"  # also test these expectations
/olhos marcar http://127.0.0.1:3080/                # capture now and store it as the good reference
/olhos ultima http://127.0.0.1:3080/                # drift only, no new capture
/olhos achar "login screen with an error"           # find an old capture by meaning
/olhos ajuda
```

Expectations should be short, concrete and visible. "The panel shows three
session cards" works; "the layout is nice" does not.

A threshold passed to the tool (`limiar`) is stored for that target in
`limiar.json` and used on the following calls.

## Configuration

Every path is configurable and the defaults derive from your home directory, so
nothing is tied to a specific machine. Override by environment variable or by the
config of the `olhos` line in your profile patch. A patch replaces the whole
config of the line, so restate every key you want to keep.

| Config key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `capturas` | `temporarios/olhos` inside the package | where captures, references and per-target `limiar.json` live. A relative path resolves inside the package; use an absolute path to keep captures across plugin updates |
| `limiar` | `0.7344` | cosine threshold for written expectations. Calibrated, not portable |
| `navegador` | `casa` | `casa` attaches to Chrome on CDP 9222; `proprio` launches a disposable headless browser |

| Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `OLHOS_GEMMA_RAIZ` | `~/workspaces/tools/embeddinggemma` | engine checkout used by `olhos.py` |
| `OLHOS_CDP` | `http://127.0.0.1:9222` | CDP endpoint |
| `OLHOS_CHROME` | `google-chrome` | browser binary for `navegador: proprio` |
| `OLHOS_PERFIL` | `<package>/temporarios/<date>-olhos/chrome-perfil` | profile directory for the disposable browser |
| `OLHOS_LIMIAR` | `0.7344` | default when the engine scripts are called directly |
| `OLHOS_LARGURA`, `OLHOS_ALTURA` | `1440`, `900` | capture viewport |

Profile patch example (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: olhos
  config:
    capturas: '/home/you/.dsh/olhos'
    limiar: 0.7344
    navegador: casa
```

## Verification

From a clone of the repository:

```sh
node --test tests/
scripts/olhos.sh selftest
```

`node --test` needs only Node.js: 20 tests covering the tool and command
registration, the bundle contract, the strict threshold decision and the
per-target key.

`scripts/olhos.sh selftest` needs the engine virtualenv installed (not the model
weights) and checks the threshold math without loading the model.

To verify the install, check the `--dump-config` output above and ask the agent
to run `olhos_verificar` against a page that is open in your browser.

## Measured results

The default threshold and the warnings below come from a calibration run on this
plugin: 20 written expectations, 22 captures, 440 labeled pairs, EmbeddingGemma,
768 dimensions.

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| expectations, all pairs | **390/440 = 88.6%** agreement at `0.7344` |
| calibration split (12 expectations) | 224/264 = 84.9%, 0 false positives, 40 false negatives |
| validation split (8 expectations) | 166/176 = 94.3%, 0 false positives, 10 false negatives |
| whole-screen drift, 10 meaningful changes | **1/10 caught** |
| whole-screen drift, 3 deliberate breakages | **1/3 caught** |
| whole-screen drift, 10 cosmetic changes | 1/10 flagged |
| pixel-difference baseline, same set | 10/10 and 3/3 caught, but 7/10 cosmetics flagged |

The threshold is the highest negative score (`max(negativos)`): no false
expectation passes it, which is why false positives are zero. The price is false
negatives: true statements whose score falls below the threshold are reported as
not found. In a live verification on the calibration page, the panel really had the
three cards and scored `0.7225`, below `0.7344`.

The drift margin on that set is negative: the two groups overlap. A whole-screen
cosine flagged a header path change and missed the three cards disappearing.
That is why drift is opt-in and never a verdict on its own.

## Limits

- **The threshold is calibrated, not portable.** It belongs to the
  EmbeddingGemma space and to a calibration set. Do not reuse a threshold
  measured for another model: the cosine range is different. Calibrate with
  `scripts/olhos.sh calibrar --positivos <file

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: a sidebar chip that lists archived conversations and restores them, for harnesses whose session list has no archive row.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-arquivadas

An **Archived sessions** chip for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness),
for harness versions whose sidebar has no archive row.

Newer harness releases moved archived conversations out of the session list and
into a filter menu (**View options → Filter sessions**). The archive still works,
but the button you used to click is gone. This plugin puts a chip in the sidebar
foot, next to the other global actions:

- the **count** of archived conversations, always visible;
- click it to **list them by title**;
- **Restore** puts one back into the session list, through the harness's own
  unarchive operation.

Nothing is copied or reimplemented from the product: the count comes from the
`workspaces` service snapshot, the titles from the `sessions` snapshot, and
restore calls `unarchiveSession` on the `uiWorkspace` service. The list filter
preference is left alone.

## Requirements

- **Node.js** `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`.
- **pnpm** on `PATH`; the harness manages profile plugins with it.
- A harness version that exposes the client services `workspaces`, `sessions`
  and `uiWorkspace`, and the `sidebar.footer.action` slot. Verified on Harness
  `0.2.0-rc.2`; the `0.1.5` line exposes the same services and slot but keeps
  its own archive row, so the chip is redundant there.

## Install

From GitHub, into a profile (`web` in the examples):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-arquivadas
dsh web            # restart the web server so the bundle loads
```

If pnpm asks for build permission (it does not for this package, which has no
native dependencies), follow the hint it prints.

## How it looks

A small archive icon with the number of archived sessions sits in the sidebar
foot. Clicking opens a panel pinned above it:

```
Sessões arquivadas            ×
──────────────────────────────
Conversa antiga     [Restaurar]
Outra conversa      [Restaurar]
```

The empty state says there is nothing archived. Escape, the ×, or a click
outside closes the panel.

## Uninstall

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-arquivadas
```

If the profile keeps the line in `dsh.profile.bundles`, remove `dsh-arquivadas`
from that list too.

## Notes

- The chip renders in the sidebar foot on purpose: in the newer shell the
  workspace list region belongs to the product's own registrant, and no slot is
  published above the session rows. The foot is where the global session actions
  already live, one row above the workspace browser's old archive row.
- Restoring an archived conversation only changes the sidebar list; the session
  log is untouched.
- No telemetry, no network calls, no host routes. The host half is an empty
  module.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

plugins.description: Voice copilot for DeepSeek Harness: names and attaches the push-to-talk session, adds composer microphones, and runs a real-time spoken conversation loop with Silero VAD, speculative transcription, streaming TTS and speaker verification.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-voz-copilot

Voice copilot for DeepSeek Harness. It gives the push-to-talk session a **name**
and a **place in the sidebar**, adds **dictation microphones to the composer**,
and can run a **real-time spoken conversation**: the microphone stays open, a
Silero VAD decides when you speak, transcription starts while you are still
silent, and the answer is spoken back sentence by sentence while the model is
still writing.

The plugin is the glue between the harness and a speech stack running on
localhost. It does **not** ship a speech-to-text engine or a text-to-speech
voice; those are external services (see [Requirements](#requirements)).

## Install

```sh
npm install -g pnpm
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-plugin-voz-copilot --allow-build=onnxruntime-node
```

`--allow-build=onnxruntime-node` é obrigatório no pnpm 10+: sem ele o pnpm bloqueia o download do binário do ONNX Runtime e a instalação falha. O pacote em si não tem passo de build.
# restart the harness (stop `dsh web` and start it again)
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` installs it **and**
adds its line to the profile bundle list. The bundle layer is read at boot, so a
restart is what activates it.

If `dsh` is installed globally, use `dsh` instead of `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh`.

### Remove

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-plugin-voz-copilot
# restart the harness
```

Removing the package removes its bundle line. Conversations already named keep
their title in the session log; nothing is deleted.

## Requirements

- **Node.js** `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the same range DeepSeek Harness supports).
- **pnpm** on `PATH` (the harness manages profile plugins with it).
- **DeepSeek Harness** with the `web` profile for the interface. The `title`
  mode is used by the `acp` profile.
- **Speech-to-text**: an HTTP endpoint compatible with whisper.cpp's
  `whisper-server`, at `whisperUrl` (default `http://127.0.0.1:8178`):
  `POST /inference?response_format=json` with the audio in the multipart field
  `file`, answering `{"text": "..."}`. The server must decode WebM/Opus (an
  ffmpeg-enabled build), WAV and MP3. This plugin does not install it.
- **Optional fast engine**: `whisperFastUrl` (for example `http://127.0.0.1:8179`)
  for short conversation segments. When it is not set, the main endpoint is used.
- **Optional text-to-speech**: the `edge-tts` CLI, or a warm HTTP server. See
  [Configuration](#configuration). Without `tts`, the real-time conversation
  button stays disabled with the reason in its tooltip; dictation still works.
- **Optional speaker verification**: Python 3 with `sherpa-onnx` and `numpy`
  (`requirements.txt`). The ERes2Net model (38 MB, Apache-2.0) and the Silero
  VAD model (2.3 MB, MIT) are bundled. The speech detector uses
  `onnxruntime-node`, installed by npm.

## Use

The plugin is additive: it does not replace any harness control.

- **Push-to-talk session.** With a companion push-to-talk bridge that binds the
  Copilot key (F23 in the reference setup) and opens the session with
  `[conversa_copilot]` as the first line of the turn, this plugin pins the
  session title to `conversa_copilot` and attaches the session to the configured
  workspace, so it appears in the sidebar instead of staying invisible. The
  bridge and the key binding are not part of this package.
- **Header microphone.** Binds the conversation that is open in the GUI as the
  target of the voice. Lit means this is the voice conversation; a second click
  unbinds it. Binding writes the session id to `statePath` (the same file the
  bridge reads) and attaches the session to the workspace.
- **Sidebar footer.** Shows which conversation is receiving the voice without
  opening it.
- **Composer microphones.** Two buttons next to Send:
  - the **plain microphone** records and leaves the transcription in the draft,
    so you can edit before sending;
  - the **microphone with an arrow** records and sends the turn directly.

  Click the same button again to stop. While recording, the button becomes a red
  stop square; `Esc` or the cancel control in the floating pill aborts. The
  transcription is appended after whatever was already in the draft, never
  replacing it. An empty transcription is an error, never an empty turn.
- **Real-time conversation.** The third button opens the spoken loop on the open
  conversation: speak normally, the answer is spoken while it is written, and
  speaking over it interrupts (barge-in). The panel has pause, stop-response and
  close controls; `Esc` closes it and always releases the microphone.
- **Only your voice.** After enrolling your voice in the conversation panel,
  speaker embeddings decide whether a segment belongs to you. Audio from other
  voices is ignored before transcription. The check is fail-open: no enrollment,
  no local server, or too-short audio lets the speech through.

## How it works

Two halves, one package:

| Half | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| host | `index.js` | `title` mode pins the session title; `attach` mode links and attaches the session, and serves `/voz-copilot/api/*` |
| page | `client.js` | header button, sidebar indicator, composer microphones, recording pill and the conversation panel |
| host | `vad.js` | Silero VAD on 16 kHz PCM: speech probability with LSTM state between calls |
| host | `speaker.js` + `speaker-servidor.py` | speaker embeddings, voice profile and the cosine decision |
| host | `fala.js` | deterministic text cleanup (markdown, code, links, emoji) and sentence splitting |
| host | `tts.js` | text to MP3 through `edge-tts` or the warm server |
| host | `falar.js` | waits for the turn to finish and reads its text |

The browser never talks to the speech servers directly: the host process owns
the loopback route and enforces a local-request boundary (loopback `Host`,
same-origin `Origin`, POST for state changes, 256 KB for JSON and 16 MB for
audio). Audio and transcripts stay on localhost unless you point a configured
service at a remote address.

## Configuration

The defaults come from the package bundle patch and boot on any machine. To use
your own workspace and voice, edit the profile patch
(`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`). A patch under the same `id` replaces
the whole config of the line, so restate every key you want to keep.

```yaml
- id: voz-copilot
  config:
    mode: 'attach'
    workspace: '/path/to/your/workspace'
    title: 'conversa_copilot'
    statePath: '~/.dsh/voz-copilot.json'
    pollMs: 3000
    whisperUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:8178'
    whisperFastUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:8179'
    voz:
      persona: 'Answer in short, plain sentences that sound natural when spoken aloud.'
      maxChars: 220
    tts:
      bin: 'edge-tts'
      voice: 'en-US-AriaNeural'
      rate: '+0%'
      volume: '+0%'
      lexicon: '/path/to/tts_lexicon.py'
      python: 'python3'
      servidorQuente: 'http://127.0.0.1:8180'
      servidorQuenteScript: '/path/to/tts-servidor.py'
      servidorQuentePython: 'python3'
    orador:
      limiar: 0.5
      perfilPath: '~/.dsh/voz-perfil.json'
```

`~` is expanded in `workspace`, `statePath` and the other paths below.

| Key | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `attach` (bundle line); code default is `title` | `attach` for the `web` profile; `title` for the `acp` profile |
| `workspace` | `.` (the process working directory) | workspace that owns the voice session; set it to your workspace path |
| `title` | `conversa_copilot` | title pinned on the push-to-talk session |
| `marker` | none, required in `title` mode | first-line marker the bridge sends, e.g. `[conversa_copilot]` |
| `statePath` | `~/.dsh/voz-copilot.json` | durable link between the bridge and the session id |
| `pollMs` | `3000` | how often `attach` mode checks the link |
| `whisperUrl` | `http://127.0.0.1:8178` | whisper-server used by dictation and by the slow path |
| `whisperFastUrl` | same as `whisperUrl` | faster whisper-server for conversation segments |
| `voz.persona` | a short spoken-answer instruction | prefix prepended to each spoken turn |
|

plugins.description: KeePassXC-backed secret vault for DeepSeek Harness: store, rotate, list and use credentials without exposing them to the model context, with an optional interactive human confirmation before every credential use.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-secret-vault

A secret vault for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness),
backed by **KeePassXC**. It exposes a `vault_*` tool family to every session of a
profile so an agent can store, rotate, list and use credentials **without the
plaintext entering the model context** by default.

The database is protected by a **key file only**. No master password exists
anywhere: not in code, config, environment, argv, session logs or the model
context. Using an existing credential goes through an **interactive human
confirmation** by default, and a use that cannot be confirmed is denied
(fail-closed).

## Install

Works on Linux, macOS and WSL (the `vault_use` tool runs commands with
`/bin/bash`). Open a terminal and run:

```sh
# 1. pnpm, needed by `dsh plugin`
npm install -g pnpm

# 2. add the plugin to your `web` profile
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-secret-vault

# 3. restart the harness: the bundle layer is read at boot
#    stop `dsh web` (Ctrl+C) and start it again
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

If `dsh` is already installed globally, step 2 is
`dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-secret-vault`.

After the restart the `vault_*` tools are available to the agent. The first call
creates the vault directory, the key file and the database.

### What the install does

`dsh plugin add` runs pnpm in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/`, so the spec can be a
GitHub repo, a tarball, a local path or a registry name. Because this package
declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, the harness appends the plugin to the profile's
bundle list and the packaged `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the
`tool-secret-vault` row at every boot. Nothing else has to be enabled.

There is **no build step and no native dependency**: plain ESM using Node
built-ins plus the packages the harness already provides.

### Update and uninstall

```sh
# update: re-run the add command (it resolves the repo again), then restart
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-secret-vault   # uninstall, then restart
```

## Requirements

- **DeepSeek Harness** itself, e.g. `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`.
- **KeePassXC 2.7 or newer**, with **`keepassxc-cli` on `PATH`** (or point
  `cliPath` at it). Tested with 2.7.10.
- **Node.js** `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the range DeepSeek Harness supports).
- **pnpm** on `PATH` — installed in step 1 above.
- A POSIX shell (`/bin/bash`) for `vault_use`; on Windows use WSL.

KeePassXC is the only external program the plugin calls. If it is missing you
get `VAULT_CLI_MISSING`; install it or set `cliPath`. The package is plain ESM
plus a POSIX shell; it has been exercised on Linux with KeePassXC 2.7.10.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `vault_status` | Vault health: auth mode, number of credentials and groups, database name, directory |
| `vault_list` | Every stored credential path and every group (titles only, never values) |
| `vault_generate` | Create or rotate an entry with a strong password generated inside `keepassxc-cli` |
| `vault_store` | Store an existing credential; the value goes to the CLI over stdin |
| `vault_show` | Non-secret metadata of one entry: canonical path, username, whether a password is stored |
| `vault_reveal` | Return the plaintext of one entry — direct human turn + authorization dialog + audit reason; can be disabled |
| `vault_use` | Run one `bash -c` command with `VAULT_PASSWORD` and `VAULT_USERNAME` injected; secret occurrences in the output are redacted |
| `vault_delete` | Soft delete by default (KeePassXC Recycle Bin); `permanent: true` purges with a dated pre-purge snapshot |

Every `entry` argument accepts a **full group path** (`work/github`) or a **bare
title** (`github`). A bare title is resolved by searching every group except the
KeePassXC Recycle Bin; a unique match wins and an ambiguous match is refused with
the candidate paths, so nothing is guessed.

`vault_generate` sizes: 16 to 64 characters, default 26; `noSpecial` and
`excludeAmbiguous` are available for services with narrow password rules.

## Configuration

The plugin works with no configuration at all. Defaults:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `vaultDir` | `''` → `$DSH_HOME/vault` | Vault directory. `DSH_HOME` defaults to `~/.dsh` (from `os.homedir()`) |
| `dbName` | `secrets.kdbx` | Database file name inside `vaultDir` (no path separators) |
| `keyName` | `secrets.key` | Key file name inside `vaultDir` (no path separators) |
| `cliPath` | `keepassxc-cli` | Path or name of the KeePassXC CLI |
| `cliTimeoutMs` | `30000` | Timeout for one CLI call (2 s to 5 min) |
| `useTimeoutMs` | `180000` | Timeout for a `vault_use` command (2 s to 15 min) |
| `confirmTimeoutMs` | `180000` | How long the authorization dialog may stay unanswered before the use is denied; `0` removes the deadline (5 s to 15 min) |
| `requireConfirmation` | `true` | Interactive human confirmation before using an existing credential |
| `allowReveal` | `true` | Allow `vault_reveal` at all |
| `binGroup` | `Recycle Bin` | Name of the KeePassXC recycle-bin group (change it for a database created in another language) |

To change a value, override the row by **id** in the profile's
`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`. A patch **replaces the whole config**, so
restate every key you keep:

```yaml
- id: tool-secret-vault
  config:
    vaultDir: '/path/to/your/vault'   # or omit it to use $DSH_HOME/vault
    dbName: 'secrets.kdbx'
    keyName: 'secrets.key'
    cliPath: 'keepassxc-cli'
    cliTimeoutMs: 30000
    useTimeoutMs: 180000
    confirmTimeoutMs: 180000
    requireConfirmation: true
    allowReveal: true
    binGroup: 'Recycle Bin'
```

### Vault layout and groups

The vault is an **arbitrary KeePassXC group tree**. The plugin never creates or
assumes group names: whatever groups your database has are the ones
`vault_list` reports, and an entry path is just `group/subgroup/title`.

Create groups in the KeePassXC GUI before storing below them (the CLI `add` does
not create missing groups). A bare title with no `/` lands in the root group, so
a fresh vault is usable immediately. Titles may repeat across groups: a bare
title that matches more than one entry is refused with the candidate paths, and
the full path picks one. Everything under the recycle-bin group (`binGroup`,
default `Recycle Bin`) is hidden from `vault_list` and from title search.

### Database and key file

The plugin expects a **key-file-only** KeePassXC database. On first use it
creates `secrets.kdbx` plus a 64-byte random `secrets.key` in `vaultDir`, both
mode `0600` inside a `0700` directory, and opens the database with
`--no-password --key-file`.

To use an **existing** KeePassXC database, make sure it authenticates with a key
file only (`Database → Database Settings → Security` in the KeePassXC GUI), then
point `vaultDir`/`dbName`/`keyName` at the pair. A database that also needs a
master password is not supported by the CLI flow of this plugin.

To inspect or edit the vault by hand, open it in the KeePassXC GUI
(`Database → Open…`) and select the key file. Do that **while the harness is not
writing**: `keepassxc-cli` and the desktop app do not coordinate locks, and
saving from the GUI can overwrite a concurrent write.

**Back up both files together.** They only work as a pair; losing either one
means losing the vault, and there is no master password to recover it. Keep the
copy outside `vaultDir`.

## Security model

- **Key file only.** No master password is stored, passed, or handled. The key
  file is 64 random bytes created by the plugin with mode `0600` inside a `0700`
  directory. Permissions are re-enforced on every operation.
- **Secrets stay out of the model context by default.** `vault_generate` creates
  the password inside `keepassxc-cli`; `vault_store` sends the value over stdin;
  `vault_use` injects it into the child environment and redacts every occurrence
  from captured stdout/stderr. None of these return the value.
- **`vault_reveal` is the only deliberate plaintext path.** It needs a reason,
  a direct human turn on the top-level session agent (subagents, background jobs
  and autonomous continuat

plugins.description: Manage MCP servers and skills, and budget DeepSeek Harness context without a restart
plugins.readme_text:
# 上下文预算

管理 MCP 服务器与 Skill，控制下一轮 prompt 的工具成本。

[English](README.en.md)

每个 MCP 工具都会带完整 JSON Schema 进入请求。服务器一多，schema 会比对话更占地方。

![工具 schema 数量示意](assets/readme-schema-v2.svg)

这个插件把配置和暴露分开。配置负责服务器和 Skill，暴露负责这一轮到底带哪些 schema。

## 安装

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:jidekaixin2dian/dsh-context-budget
```

桌面端由应用管理 profile 时，请在插件管理器里安装。安装或更新 host 半后，退出并重新打开 DSH；桌面端没有浏览器式 `Ctrl+R` 硬刷新。

## 使用

打开 **设置 -> 上下文预算**。

**上下文预算** 按 MCP 服务器分组，隐藏这一轮不需要的整组 schema，随时恢复。MCP 进程继续运行。全部显示、关闭全部 MCP、关闭最大组、精简模式都在这一页。

**MCP 服务器** 新增、编辑、删除、启停，写 profile 或 global 的 `cordis.patch.yml`，HMR 生效。stdio 用 command/args/env，streamable-http 用 url/headers。

**Skills** 搜索、新建、删除、单 Skill 启停。新建可写用户或项目目录，删除移到 `.trash`。

模型工具：

```text
context_budget action=status
context_budget action=session disabled=["mcp:github", "skills"]
context_budget action=reset
```

`mcp` 是全部 MCP 的通配，`mcp:<server>` 只针对一台服务器。设置页的全局预算作用于所有会话和子代理，`action=session` 只覆盖当前会话。

## 原理

预算部分在 `agent/pre-step` 里调用 `ctx.tools.restrict({ deny })`，工具 schema 在 prompt 组装前被移除。MCP 部分按行编辑 `cordis.patch.yml`，保留无关行和注释，由 HMR 应用。Skill 部分用 rank-0 override provider 把停用项设为 `modelInvocable:false`。

token 数按序列化 schema 和 Skill 描述估算，不是模型分词器的精确值。

## 边界

- 动态 MCP 管理器把工具注册在 agent 作用域时，`ctx.tools.restrict` 隐藏不了，请用对应管理器的 unload。
- MCP CRUD 会写 `cordis.patch.yml`；手工改过该文件时，保存前先看 diff。
- Skill 的 ZIP 或文件夹导入暂未实现；只在 scoped provider 出现的 Skill 可能无法隐藏。
- host 半和 client 半更新都需要重开 DSH。

## 开发

```sh
npm test
```

9 个单元测试覆盖分组规则、MCP 行编辑和 Skill 文件操作。

[GitHub](https://github.com/jidekaixin2dian/dsh-context-budget) · [Releases](https://github.com/jidekaixin2dian/dsh-context-budget/releases) · MIT

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: live DeepSeek API peak/off-peak tariff state and spend tracking, for the agent, the chat, a sidebar chip and Settings (Windows, Linux, macOS).
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-pico-detector

DeepSeek sells its API at two rates: **PEAK** (full price) and **OFF-PEAK** (half
price). This plugin tells you which one is in effect right now, and how much the
API has cost you, inside [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).

One plugin line, four surfaces:

| Who | How | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| the agent | `pico_status` and `deepseek_spend` tools | the state now and the next transition, so it can decide to defer heavy work; the spend of the window |
| you, in the chat | `/pico` and `/gasto` commands | the same texts, read-only |
| you, in the GUI | chip in the sidebar footer | colored dot with the rate in effect, short label, countdown inside the approach window, spend of the window |
| you, in the GUI | **Settings → Pico Detector** | spend breakdown, FX rate, currency and window, next transitions, policy in effect |

**Peak rules are always evaluated in Beijing time** (the official rule). Times are
shown in **your** zone, taken from your machine; pin another zone with
`displayTimezone` (see [Configuration](#configuration)).

## Requirements

- **Node.js** `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the same range DeepSeek Harness supports).
- **pnpm** on `PATH` — the harness manages profile plugins with it.
- **DeepSeek Harness** itself, e.g. `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`.

## Install

Works the same on **Linux, macOS and Windows**. Open a terminal (PowerShell is
fine on Windows) and run:

```sh
# 1. pnpm (needed by `dsh plugin`)
npm install -g pnpm

# 2. add the plugin to your `web` profile
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-pico-detector

# 3. restart the harness: the bundle layer is read at boot
#    stop `dsh web` (Ctrl+C) and start it again
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

If `dsh` is already installed globally, step 2 is
`dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-pico-detector`.

After the restart: the chip is at the bottom of the sidebar, the tools and the
`/pico`, `/gasto` commands are live, and **Settings → Pico Detector** has the
currency and window switches.

### What the install does

`dsh plugin add` runs pnpm in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/` (on Windows,
`%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\web\`), so the spec can be a GitHub repo, a tarball,
a local path or a registry name. Because this package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`,
the harness then appends `dsh-pico-detector` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the
profile manifest — that line in the profile is the only activation, and it is
applied at every boot. Nothing else to configure.

The package has **no build step and no native dependencies**: plain ESM using only
Node built-ins (`node:zlib`, `node:fs`, `node:os`). Nothing to compile on any OS.

### Update and uninstall

```sh
# update: re-run the add command above (it resolves the repo again), then restart
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-pico-detector   # uninstall, then restart
```

## Peak policy (official)

Source: [api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing),
checked on 2026-08-23 and again on 2026-09-10 (no rule change).

The official wording is in UTC: *"Peak hours are 01:00 - 04:00 and 06:00 - 10:00
UTC, Monday through Friday (all other hours are off-peak)."* Converted to Beijing
time:

| Window | Beijing (UTC+8) |
|---|---|
| PEAK, morning (Mon–Fri) | 09:00 – 12:00 |
| PEAK, afternoon (Mon–Fri) | 14:00 – 18:00 |
| OFF-PEAK | every other hour |
| Weekend (Sat–Sun in Beijing) | all day OFF-PEAK |

The week boundary follows the **Beijing calendar**, which matters at the edges of
the day for anyone not in Beijing: the plugin computes it that way.

## States

The state names are DeepSeek's own (`peak` / `off-peak`). The UI labels are in
Portuguese.

| State | Label | Color | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `off_peak` | `OFF-PEAK (metade do preço)` | green | OFF-PEAK active, half price |
| `peak` | `PEAK (preço cheio)` | red | PEAK active, full price |
| `approaching_peak` | `PEAK EM BREVE` | amber | PEAK starts within `approachMinutes` |
| `approaching_off_peak` | `OFF-PEAK EM BREVE` | amber | PEAK ends within `approachMinutes` |

The color always means **the rate in effect**, never the incoming one: green only
while OFF-PEAK is active, red only while PEAK is active. Amber is the current rate
changing within the approach window, and then the label says which way. Default
approach window: 30 minutes (`approachMinutes`).

## Where the money number comes from

The DeepSeek API has **no usage endpoint**: `GET /user/balance` exists, and balance
is not spend (it moves with top-ups, promo credits and any other client using the
same key). What the invoice uses is the published rule `tokens × price`, and the
tokens are recorded, per model step, with the instant and the model, in the
harness's durable session ledger:

```
~/.dsh/sessions/<workspace>/<session>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd (v3 on older harnesses)
```

Each step is priced by **the model in that event** and by **the tariff in effect
at that event's instant** (not at query time, which would be wrong on every day
that crosses a window boundary), with the three buckets priced differently: input
without cache, cache read and output.

| Model | Input (1M) | Cache read (1M) | Output (1M) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-flash` | US$ 0.15 / 0.30 | US$ 0.003 / 0.006 | US$ 0.60 / 1.20 |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` | US$ 0.66 / 1.32 | US$ 0.022 / 0.044 | US$ 1.98 / 3.96 |

(off-peak / peak; off-peak is half price. Source:
[api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing),
checked 2026-10-07.)

**What the number does not cover, and the UI says so:** LLM calls outside the agent
loop (session titles, web search) record the request but not tokens, so the total
is a **floor**. A model missing from the price table is priced as Flash and
**flagged as such**. An unreadable session log is counted as an error and shown,
never summed as zero.

**Exchange rate:** a chain of keyless public sources (awesomeapi → frankfurter →
open.er-api), first one to answer wins and is named in the result; 30-minute cache.
If all fail, the last reading is shown marked stale with its age and the reason; if
there was never a reading, the total stays in USD instead of inventing a number.

**Refresh cadence:** the rate is checked every 10 s (pure computation) and the
spend every 60 s (incremental disk read; ~1.3 ms in the steady state).

## Configuration

Everything falls back to a sane default: a wrong config never breaks the detector.
Override by `id` in your profile patch (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`). A
patch **replaces the whole config of the line**, so restate every key you want to
keep:

```yaml
- id: pico-detector
  config:
    policy:
      timezone: 'Asia/Shanghai'
      peakWindows: [['09:00', '12:00'], ['14:00', '18:00']]
      weekendOffpeak: true
    displayTimezone: 'Europe/Lisbon'        # omit to use your machine's zone
    approachMinutes: 30
    spend:
      interval: 'today'                     # today | 24h | 7d | 30d | month
      currency: 'BRL'                       # any ISO-4217 code
```

## Troubleshooting

- **`pnpm not found on PATH`** — `npm install -g pnpm`, then re-run the command.
- **Plugin installed but nothing appears** — restart the harness; the bundle layer
  is read at boot, not at install time.
- **Spend shows 0 while sessions exist** — the ledger lives under `$DSH_HOME`
  (default `~/.dsh`). If you moved it, set `DSH_HOME` or the `spend.home` config.
- **pnpm blocks a build script** — it does not for this package: there is no
  `prepare`/build script. (A git-hosted dependency with one would need an
  `allowBuilds` entry.)
- **Wrong time zone** — the default is your machine's zone; pin another with
  `displayTimezone` (see above).

## Verification

The package ships its own check suite. Run it on the installed copy, which has the
harness packages around it:

```sh
node ~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/dsh-pico-detector/lib/selfcheck.mjs
# on Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\web\node_modules\dsh-pico-detector\lib\selfcheck.mjs
```

It covers the peak policy (windows, exact boundaries, weeke

plugins.description: 一个轻量的 macOS 桌面应用壳，Rust 编写，承载 DeepSeek Harness WebUI，一键启停
plugins.readme_text:
# DeepSeek Harness (macOS 桌面壳)

一个**轻量**的 macOS 桌面应用壳（[Tauri 2](https://v2.tauri.app/)），承载本机
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) WebUI：

- 一键启动：打开应用即拉起 `dsh web`，窗口内直接显示 `http://127.0.0.1:3080`
  上的完整 UI（与浏览器版同一份 `~/.dsh` 数据）
- **托盘常驻**：关闭窗口只隐藏，服务继续在后台跑；点托盘/ Dock 图标一键重新打开
- **通知弹窗**：首次转入后台、后台就绪、异常退出都有系统通知
- **彻底退出才关端口**：只有菜单/托盘里的"退出"（或 Cmd+Q）会杀掉 dsh 进程树并退出
- 智能端口：3080 已有 dsh 在跑则直接挂接；被其他程序占用则自动换系统分配端口
- 集成 [dsh-better-sidebar](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar)
  （VSCode 风格侧边栏）— 首次运行自动安装到 web profile
- [Anthropic Codex 配色](https://github.com/miniLV/Anthropic-codex-theme)
  （`#F8F6F1`/`#1E1D1B` + 铜色 `#CA7554`）— 通过内置 client 插件注入 DSH 设计 token
- **毛玻璃半透明**：窗口叠加 macOS vibrancy（frosted glass），主题 token 以
  半透明 rgba 呈现；进入全屏自动切换为不透明（Rust 轮询 `is_fullscreen` 并
  通过 `data-desktop-fullscreen` 属性联动页面）
- **鲸鱼图标**：Dock 应用图标与菜单栏（状态栏）图标为定制设计的鲸鱼图标
  （`src-tauri/icons/dock_icon.svg` / `menu_bar_icon.svg`，由原图转制的
  SVG 源文件；`dock_icon.png`/`menu_bar_icon.png` 为原始位图）。菜单栏图标
  为单色 template 图（`icons/tray-icon.png`），随系统明暗自适应
- **启动速度优化**：复用系统 node/dsh（不捆绑运行时）、boot 页为纯静态 HTML
  （窗口秒开）、服务与窗口并行启动、插件存在时零额外进程开销、release 构建
  `lto + codegen-units=1 + opt-level=s + strip`

## 架构

```
┌─ Tauri 应用 (Rust + WKWebView) ──────────────────────────────┐
│ 本地 boot 页（启动/就绪/错误/日志，Anthropic 配色）            │
│   └─ 就绪后跳转 → http://127.0.0.1:<port>（真正的界面）       │
│ 服务管理器 (src/server.rs)                                    │
│   定位 node/dsh → 探测 3080 → 准备插件 → 拉起 dsh web         │
│   → 从 stdout 解析真实 URL → 监视进程 → 退出时杀进程组         │
│ 插件管理 (src/plugins.rs)                                     │
│   dsh-better-sidebar + dsh-anthropic-theme → web profile      │
│ 原生菜单/托盘 (src/menu.rs)                                   │
└───────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                            │ 拉起
                   ┌────────▼────────┐
                   │  dsh web 服务    │  数据 → ~/.dsh
                   └─────────────────┘
```

安全模型与参考实现一致：harness 页面作为纯远程页面加载，**不授予** Tauri IPC
访问权限（不开 `dangerousRemoteDomainIpcAccess`），外壳操作全走原生菜单/托盘。

## 开发

前置：Rust、Node ≥ 22、pnpm、本机已安装 `@deepseek-ai/dsh`（`dsh web` 可跑）。

```bash
npm install          # @tauri-apps/cli
npm run dev          # tauri dev（窗口 + 服务）
npm run build        # release 构建 → src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/DeepSeek Harness.app
```

### 环境变量覆盖项

| 变量 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `DSH_DESKTOP_NODE` | 指定 node 可执行文件绝对路径（默认 PATH → Homebrew → nvm） |
| `DSH_DESKTOP_DSH_BIN` | 指定 dsh `lib/bin.js` 绝对路径 |
| `DSH_DESKTOP_PNPM` | 指定 pnpm 绝对路径（插件安装用） |
| `DSH_DESKTOP_THEME_DIR` | 指定内置主题插件目录（默认打包资源 / dev checkout） |
| `DSH_DESKTOP_PORT` | 默认绑定端口（默认 3080；同时跑多个实例时用） |
| `DSH_DESKTOP_CWD` | dsh 服务进程工作目录（默认用户主目录） |
| `DSH_HOME` | 透传；harness 数据根目录（默认 `~/.dsh`） |

## 插件（自动准备，仅缺时安装）

- `dsh-better-sidebar@0.12.1` — npm registry，装进 `~/.dsh/profiles/web` 并注册
  bundle（`dsh plugin --profile web add` 自动协调）
- `dsh-anthropic-theme` — 本仓库 `plugins/anthropic-theme/`，以 `file:` 本地包
  形式安装；主题通过 client 插件覆盖 DSH 的 `--dsw-static-*` 设计 token
  （`body` / `body[data-ds-dark-theme]`），light/dark 双套配色 + DM Sans /
  JetBrains Mono 字体栈

改动主题后记得**递增 `plugins/anthropic-theme/package.json` 的 version**——
应用按版本号判断是否需要重装（`file:` 包不自动跟随源码变化）。

## 图标

图标源文件：`src-tauri/icons/dock_icon.png`（Dock，白底蓝鲸）与
`menu_bar_icon.png`（菜单栏，透明底黑鲸），另有同名 `.svg`（内嵌原图，无损转制）。

重新生成全部图标格式（PNG + ICNS + tray）：

```bash
python3 scripts/gen-icons.py src-tauri/icons/dock_icon.png src-tauri/icons/menu_bar_icon.png src-tauri/icons
```

## 测试

```bash
npm run build
# 手动测试（见 README 测试清单）：
#   1. 打开应用 → boot 页 → 自动跳转 UI
#   2. 关窗口 → 托盘常驻 + 首次通知；lsof -i :3080 仍在
#   3. 点托盘/Dock → 窗口回来，端口保持
#   4. 托盘右键 → 退出 → 进程退出、端口关闭（lsof -i :3080 无输出）
```

## 参考

- [xiincs/deepseek-harness-desktop](https://github.com/xiincs/deepseek-harness-desktop) — 架构蓝本（Windows 向）
- [omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar) — 侧边栏插件
- [miniLV/Anthropic-codex-theme](https://github.com/miniLV/Anthropic-codex-theme) — 配色

plugins.description: A personal gallery of plugins for DeepSeek Harness
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH Plugin Gallery

A personal collection of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> These plugins currently target DSH `0.1.0-rc.6`. DSH is prerelease software, so extension APIs and page structure may change between versions.

## Gallery

| Plugin | Package | Runtime | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Mobile Sidebar](plugins/mobile-sidebar) | `@yfzhou/dsh-mobile-sidebar` | Web client | Removes the collapsed rail on small screens and adds a hamburger beside the conversation title. |
| [Full-width Chat](plugins/full-width-chat) | `@yfzhou/dsh-full-width-chat` | Web client | Lets conversations use the full available content width. |
| [Session Cost Statusline](plugins/session-cost-statusline) | `@yfzhou/dsh-session-cost-statusline` | Web client | Adds an estimated CNY cost before the standard session statistics. |
| [Touch Tooltips](plugins/touch-tooltips) | `@yfzhou/dsh-touch-tooltips` | Web client | Suppresses tooltip bubbles on touch devices, where a tap would otherwise leave them stuck on screen. |
| [Codex Moot Escalation](plugins/codex-moot-escalation) | `@yfzhou/dsh-codex-moot-escalation` | Host | Removes impossible escalation arguments for Codex sessions already running with unrestricted sandbox access. |
| [Codex Subscription](plugins/codex-subscription) | `@yfzhou/dsh-llm-codex-subscription` | Host | Adds a Codex provider that reuses the local Codex CLI login for ChatGPT subscription models. |
| [Codex Usage](plugins/codex-usage) | `@yfzhou/dsh-codex-usage` | Host + Web client | Shows manual Codex subscription usage and reset time inside Codex conversations. |

## Installation

Install a plugin into a DSH profile using the DSH plugin command:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @yfzhou/dsh-mobile-sidebar
```

Every gallery package is a self-contained DSH bundle. The command installs the dependency and automatically adds its `cordis.bundle.yml` patch to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` stack. Do not add a duplicate row to `cordis.patch.yml`.

For local development, pass a `file:` package specifier instead of a bare
path. This copies the package into the profile and installs its declared
dependencies (a bare path is treated as a pnpm link, which does not install
dependencies for packages such as Codex Usage):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add file:./plugins/mobile-sidebar
```

Upgrade installed plugins with `dsh plugin --profile web update`. Restart a persistent DSH service after changing its profile. Browser plugins also require a page refresh after first installation or upgrade.

## Personal presets

Version-controlled personal agent compositions live under [`presets/`](presets/). They are separate from publishable plugins because DSH discovers them as complete directories under `$DSH_HOME/.agent-presets`. See [`presets/README.md`](presets/README.md) for the local symlink setup and portability notes.

## Development

This is a pnpm workspace with one independently publishable package per directory.

```bash
pnpm check
pnpm pack:dry-run
```

The repository contains prebuilt plain-JavaScript client modules because DSH loads browser plugin entry points directly. There is no TypeScript or bundling step in this repository.

## Publishing status

The packages are prepared for npm publication but are not necessarily published yet. Pin exact versions in production profiles once releases exist.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: DSH 插件：模型在知识库目录执行 grep/glob 搜索时，自动补充 QMD 语义检索结果 DSH plugin: auto-supplement QMD semantic search when the model greps/globs a knowledge-base directory
plugins.readme_text:
# qmd-autosearch

自动补搜插件：当模型在知识库目录执行 `grep` / `glob` 搜索时，自动补充一次 QMD 语义检索，并把结果注入模型上下文。

DeepSeek Harness 插件（`dsh-plugin`）。零外部依赖。

## 功能

- **自动触发**：模型在 QMD 集合对应的目录内执行 `grep` / `glob`（顶层调用）即触发，无需显式调用
- **语义补搜**：QMD 单次查询（lex + vec，服务端 LLM 重排），检索范围限定在配置的 collections
- **智能查询词**：以最近的用户消息（任务要求）为语义主查询；消息过短或与搜索主题无关时，回退使用 grep pattern
- **异步注入**：结果排队到 `agent.inbox.nextStep`，下一个 pre-step 注入模型上下文，不阻塞当前工具调用
- **防重复**：同一 agent 内相同（工具、路径、pattern）签名只补搜一次
- **容错**：QMD 服务不可用或查询无结果时静默跳过，不影响原流程

## 工作原理

```
grep/glob 执行完成 → tools/result 钩子
  → 路径在触发范围内（由 QMD status 解析的集合路径）？
  → QMD query（collections 限定 + LLM 重排）
  → 结果排队 agent.inbox.nextStep
  → 下一个 pre-step 注入模型上下文（user 角色 system-reminder 风格）
```

## 安装

### 方式一：npm 安装（发布后可用）

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add qmd-autosearch
```

### 方式二：本地路径引用（开发调试）

在 `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` 的 insert 列表追加：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: qmd-autosearch
      name: 'file:///path/to/qmd-autosearch/index.js'
      config:
        qmdUrl: http://localhost:6179/mcp
        collections:
          - knowledge-concepts-keynes
          - knowledge-principles-keynes
        limit: 5
        minScore: 25
```

## 配置

| 配置项 | 必填 | 默认值 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `qmdUrl` | ✅ | 无 | QMD MCP 服务地址（如 `http://localhost:6179/mcp`） |
| `collections` | ✅ | 无 | 搜索范围：QMD 集合名列表（`qmd collection list` 可查） |
| `limit` | 否 | `5` | 注入结果的条数上限 |
| `minScore` | 否 | `25` | 最低匹配度过滤（百分数，低于此值的命中丢弃） |
| `triggerRoots` | 否 | 自动 | 触发判断的文件系统根路径列表；缺省时从 QMD `status` 动态解析集合路径 |

> 未配置 `qmdUrl` / `collections` 时插件禁用并输出 warn 日志。

## 使用

插件**全自动运行，无需手动调用**。配置完成后，正常使用 DSH 即可：

1. 让模型在知识库目录内搜索（如 `grep 某个概念`）
2. 插件检测到搜索发生在 QMD 集合目录内，自动补充一次语义检索
3. 结果作为补充提示注入模型的下一步上下文，模型可据此用 `read` 读取命中文档正文

### 效果示例

模型执行 `grep 内需` 后，下一步上下文中会出现：

```text
<system-reminder>
QMD 语义检索补充：你在知识库目录执行了「grep 内需」，系统已自动用语义检索（范围限定 QMD 集合，LLM 重排）补搜，查询词「内需」。结果如下（docid 映射为绝对路径后用 read 读取正文）：

Found 3 results for "内需":
#abc123 85% <collection>/concepts/<file>.md - <标题>
#def456 42% <collection>/principles/<file>.md - <标题>
...
</system-reminder>
```

### 验证插件已生效

- 让模型在集合目录内 grep 一个词，观察下一步是否出现上述补充消息
- 或查看宿主日志中的 `qmd-autosearch: 触发路径池（来自 QMD 集合）N 个`（插件启动后首次触发时输出）

## 前置条件

- 运行中的 QMD MCP 服务（`qmd mcp --http --port 6179`）
- 已建立至少一个 collection（`qmd collection add <name> <path>`）

## License

MIT

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-safeguard

面向 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）的危险命令 + 密钥泄漏拦截插件。挂载到 `tools/pre-execute` waterfall，在工具解析前短路拒绝，被拦截的副作用不会发生。

## 简介

- **危险命令拦截**：对 `bash` 工具的命令做正则匹配，命中即 `deny`。
- **密钥泄漏拦截**：对所有工具的 arguments 做 `JSON.stringify` 后扫描常见密钥模式，命中即 `deny`。
- **可配置**：危险/密钥检测开关、额外正则、精确豁免名单。
- **两个辅助工具**：`guard_list`（列出当前规则）与 `guard_check`（纯检查不拦截，供调试/自检）。

> 重要：本插件是**基于正则的启发式拦截**，不验签、不识别密钥真伪、不做沙箱隔离。它无法替代密钥扫描器、签名校验或操作系统级沙箱，只能拦截明显的高风险动作。

## 安装

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-safeguard
```

本地开发安装：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add file:./plugins/dsh-safeguard
```

## 默认规则表

### 危险命令（`enableDanger`）

| 规则名 | 匹配内容 |
|---|---|
| rm -rf | `rm -rf` / `rm -fr` 且目标是 `/`、`*`、`./`、`../`、`.`, `~`、`$HOME` |
| git push --force | `git push --force` / `--force-with-lease` / `-f` |
| git reset --hard | `git reset --hard` |
| git clean -fd | `git clean` 带 `-fd` / `-df` 等同时含 f、d 的标志 |
| chmod -R 777 | `chmod -R 777` |
| mkfs | `mkfs` / `mkfs.ext4` 等 |
| dd 写盘 | `dd if=... of=/dev/...` |
| 重定向到块设备 | `> /dev/sd[a-z]` |
| curl\|sh 管道执行 | `curl ... \| sh`、`wget ... \| bash` 等 |
| SQL DROP | 以 `DROP TABLE/DATABASE/INDEX/...` 开头 |
| SQL DELETE | 以 `DELETE FROM` 开头 |
| SQL TRUNCATE | 以 `TRUNCATE [TABLE] ...` 开头 |

### 密钥泄漏（`enableSecrets`）

| 规则名 | 匹配模式 |
|---|---|
| AWS Access Key (AKIA) | `AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}` |
| sk- API Key | `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}` |
| GitHub PAT (ghp_) | `ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}` |
| GitHub Fine-grained PAT (github_pat_) | `github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{10,}` |
| PEM 私钥 | `-----BEGIN (RSA\|OPENSSH\|EC\|PGP) PRIVATE KEY-----` |
| Slack Token (xox-) | `xox[baprs]-...` |

> `eyJ` 开头的长 JWT **不拦截**（模式太宽，误报率高）。

## 配置项

在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`（或 bundle 配置）中覆盖：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: guard
      name: dsh-safeguard
      config:
        enableDanger: true      # 危险命令拦截开关（默认 true）
        enableSecrets: true     # 密钥泄漏拦截开关（默认 true）
        extraPatterns:          # 额外正则字符串（额外危险命令规则）
          - 'curl.*\|.*bash'
        allowList:              # 精确豁免名单（字符串完全一致才豁免）
          - 'rm -rf /tmp/safe-dir'
```

| 配置项 | 类型 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enableDanger` | boolean | `true` | 是否拦截危险命令 |
| `enableSecrets` | boolean | `true` | 是否拦截密钥泄漏 |
| `extraPatterns` | string[] | `[]` | 额外危险命令正则（非法正则以警告跳过） |
| `allowList` | string[] | `[]` | 精确豁免：危险命令按整条命令、密钥按命中片段做完全一致匹配 |

## 两个工具的用法

### `guard_list`

无参，列出当前启用的规则类别与条目数：

```
[dsh-safeguard] 规则清单
危险命令: 启用（12 条规则）
密钥检测: 启用（6 条规则）
额外正则: 0 条
豁免名单: 0 条
```

### `guard_check`

参数 `text`（必填 string）。纯检查不拦截，返回命中规则名 / 类别 / 是否豁免：

- `guard_check("rm -rf /")` → 命中，类别 `danger`，规则 `rm -rf`
- `guard_check("aws key: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE")` → 命中，类别 `secrets`，规则 `AWS Access Key (AKIA)`
- `guard_check("echo hello")` → 通过

模型可通过 `await tools.guard_check({ text: "..." })` 做程序化自检。

## 不验签、不做沙箱替代

- 本插件只做**正则模式匹配**，不校验密钥真实性，也不校验命令签名。
- 它**不是沙箱**：不会隔离文件系统、网络或子进程，拦截的是「命中明显高风险模式」的调用。
- 生产环境仍应配合密钥扫描器（如 gitleaks、trufflehog）、签名校验与操作系统级沙箱（如 `dsh-bash-sandbox`）使用。

## License

MIT
